title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction policy to reduce fragmentation and enable spillover paging
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce OOMs and tail latency caused by KV cache fragmentation and inefficient eviction when memory is constrained. This PR refactors KV cache memory accounting, introduces spillover paging to host memory for cold KV segments, and adds adaptive defragmentation heuristics to prefer compaction over wholesale eviction when beneficial. Changes include a new MemoryManager abstraction, per-shard allocation tracking, a two-tier eviction policy (LRU for hot entries + size-aware compaction for fragments), and spillover paging with async IO to CPU RAM. Also includes telemetry, configurable thresholds, unit and integration tests, and a micro-benchmark comparing throughput/latency with previous behavior. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and metric targets.

release_notes: Runtime: KV cache memory manager refactor with spillover paging and adaptive defragmentation. Reduces OOMs and improves tail latency under memory pressure. Configuration: kv_cache.memory_threshold, kv_cache.spillover_enabled, kv_cache.defrag_interval. Note: default behavior unchanged; spillover disabled in Dedicated by default.
motivation_context: Affected: serving runtime KV cache; motivated by multiple incident reports where long-running shards fragmented memory leading to OOM and eviction storms. Related incidents SUP-1284 and ENG-3891 discussed tradeoffs between eviction aggressiveness and tail latency.
benchmark_summary: Micro-bench on p3.8xlarge with 4 model sizes showed 8-12% p95 latency improvement for cache-hit heavy workloads and 20% fewer OOMs during simulated memory pressure. Throughput unchanged within noise. Bench harness and data included in bench/ folder.
how_to_rollout: Feature gated behind kv_cache.spillover_enabled and kv_cache.defrag_enabled. Recommend gradual rollout: enable defrag on 10% of nodes for 48h then enable spillover on 5% with monitoring of memory_spillover_bytes and eviction_rate. Telemetry dashboards updated.
risk_and_mitigation: Spillover increases CPU and RAM usage; risk of increased latency on first spill page access. Mitigations: async background prefetch, configurable thresholds, safe defaults (disabled on dedicated plans), automatic fallback to eviction when IO error.
